request: What did CRS report about Medicare prescription drug price negotiation and its expected savings?

reply.reply:
CRS reported that CBO projected Medicare drug-price negotiation would reduce federal Medicare drug spending by **$25 billion in 2031**. This is a forecast, not realized savings; CRS’s report dated December 8, 2023, attributes it specifically to the negotiation provisions, not all IRA drug provisions. (CRS R47872, PDF p. 15)

CRS also reported CBO’s forecast that average Part D net prices would be 9% lower and Part B net prices 8% lower in 2031. Separately, CBO projected net prices for selected negotiated drugs would be about 50% lower on average; that price estimate is distinct from the federal spending savings figure. (CRS R47872, PDF p. 15)
